newsitem.title: USA: Clinton approves U.S. force to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Clinton approves U.S. force to Zaire.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has agreed in principle to order U.S. troops to participate "in limited fashion" with an international rescue mission for Zaire, the White House said on Wednesday.
White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said the U.S. commitment would involve several thousand troops, which would be deployed for a four-month period.
He said 1,000 ground troops would be sent to Zaire and several thousand other troops would be sent to the region to supply support activities.

McCurry said that detailed consultations have "led the president to decide that the United States is willing in principle" to participate "in a limited fashion in a humanitarian mission as long as certain conditions are stipulated to."

Among the conditions McCurry listed were that the mission would be of limited duration and that the mission would be made up of a multinational force. He said the U.S. forces would serve under an American commander.

McCurry also said the mission would have to be "very clearly defined" and it would not try to disarm militants or conduct any kind of "forced entry." The countries in the region would have to give their consent, he said.
